extracted.intended_audience: authors with a finished draft seeking a professional manuscript assessment (fiction and narrative non-fiction writers)
extracted.subtask_description: A commercial manuscript assessment service providing a full structural editorial report on an entire book-length manuscript (fiction and narrative non-fiction), with actionable feedback, commercial-readiness advice, and optional follow-up support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive structural feedback on the entire manuscript, covering overall structure and how the book is organised.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors provide insights on key elements such as structure, plot, pacing, writing style, characterisation, and marketability. The service is pitched as a 'full manuscript assessment' to identify big-picture structural problems and show how to elevate the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of plot: whether the story works, where plot holes exist, and what needs reworking to make the manuscript function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors 'tease out what needs to be done to make a manuscript work' and will point out plot bumps, missing beats or structural fixes required to strengthen the narrative and agent-readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pacing and tension
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of pacing at both sentence-by-sentence and whole-manuscript levels, and how tension is built and sustained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors comment on pace and tension (some have 'an incredible eye for pace and tension, both on a sentence-by-sentence level and across the entirety of your manuscript'). Examples of feedback include suggestions to tighten sentences, move or integrate backstory, and highlight where tension is diminished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characterisation / character development
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed, character-by-character assessment of how well characters are drawn and developed throughout the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports may address which characters to focus on, how to deepen or slim character arcs, and may include chapter-by-chapter notes on character performance and consistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing style and sentence-level craft
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback on prose, sentence construction, word choice, tone and overall writing style.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors provide examples of rewritten sentences to be 'cleaner and leaner', give tips for word choice, and sometimes supply specific edits of text as examples to illustrate improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dialogue
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of dialogue quality, authenticity, and how dialogue serves characterization and pacing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors comment on dialogue as part of broader notes on pace and character, and may suggest techniques to improve conversations and use dialogue to reveal information rather than exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Point of view (POV)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the manuscript's use of perspective(s) and any POV-related problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports note POV changes and their effects on clarity and reader engagement (e.g., identifying when a change of viewpoint causes issues and recommending fixes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting
rubrics_metrics.description: Feedback on how setting is used and whether it effectively supports story, character and tone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors assess how setting contributes to atmosphere, plot plausibility and immersion, and may suggest ways to strengthen or economise description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre suitability and expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the manuscript meets the conventions and expectations of its genre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors are matched by genre expertise and provide genre-specific tips, recommended reading, and notes on where the manuscript aligns or diverges from market expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Marketability / commercial potential
rubrics_metrics.description: An evaluation of the manuscript's commercial viability and advice on its chances in the market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors offer advice on marketability and, if a manuscript is judged 'submission ready' and shows strong commercial potential, Jericho Writers may provide free advice on agent submission packs, access to AgentMatch, and in some cases agent approaches. This referral service is reserved for manuscripts editors believe have strong commercial potential and very high quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length and wordcount considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Price and report scope are determined by wordcount; editors consider manuscript length as part of their assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clients select wordcount for a quote. Editorial reports are usually around 3,500 words (range 2,500–4,000 depending on manuscript length). Pricing tiers and service suitability reference wordcount (e.g., opening section review for first 20,000 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Chapter-by-chapter analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed, chapter-level commentary as part of the full editorial report where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some editors provide chapter-by-chapter notes, character-by-character breakdowns, and thorough coverage 'missing nothing'—useful for pinpointing issues and action points at the micro-structure level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actionable feedback and remediation steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Reports should give clear, actionable steps to resolve problems, with examples and practical advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial reports typically include concrete next steps, sample rewrites, tips for the genre, recommended reading lists, links to technique articles, and a 'blueprint' for taking a manuscript from raw to publishable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission formatting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifications for how authors should format and submit manuscripts for editing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only upload Word documents; number pages; double-space lines; use an easy-to-read font such as Times New Roman 12; indent paragraphs; use page breaks throughout. These formatting requirements help editors read and mark up manuscripts efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service suitability by draft stage (which edit to choose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on which editorial service is appropriate depending on the manuscript's stage (e.g., manuscript assessment vs developmental edit vs line-editing/copy-editing/proofreading).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript assessment is ideal for a finished draft or early drafts to identify big-picture issues; developmental edits (with in-text comments) are recommended for later-stage manuscripts that need detailed restructuring; line-editing/copy-editing/proofreading are for sentence-level polishing nearer publication. The page recommends self-editing first to present the best possible draft to an editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery time / turnaround expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected timeframes for delivery of editorial reports and different service levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard manuscript assessment turnaround is around 3–4 weeks; express manuscript assessment is around 2 weeks; developmental editing typically takes about 6 weeks. Matching with an editor takes ~2–4 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up support and further editorial work
rubrics_metrics.description: Availability of follow-up contact and options for additional mentoring or post-editorial support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After receiving the report clients can clarify questions via email and may book further one-to-one mentoring sessions. Developmental edits include an email exchange equivalent to 1 hour; manuscript assessment includes a short email exchange. Clients can also request additional mentoring exclusive to editorial clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor selection and matching criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: How editors are chosen and matched to manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matching considers editor experience, genres of interest and whether the editor feels they are the right fit. Editors are freelance, so availability affects matches. Clients may request a shortlist of 4–5 preferred editors, but exact matches cannot be guaranteed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of illustrations for picture books
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on submitting picture books with illustrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors may include illustrations when submitting picture books so an editor can review them, but illustrations are not essential; in traditional publishing an imprint may provide its own illustrator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope exclusions / unsuitability (academic texts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Types of works not suitable for this manuscript assessment service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The service accepts manuscripts of all genres including children's fiction and non-fiction but is not suitable for academic texts.
